question: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic. Which of these terms were added to the Preamble by the 42nd constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Socialist, Secular**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, added the words **"Socialist" and "Secular"** to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The addition of "Socialist" emphasized the government's commitment to reducing inequality and achieving social justice.
 
• The inclusion of "Secular" highlighted the state's impartiality towards all religions, ensuring equal treatment and freedom of religion.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the "Mini Constitution" due to its significant impact on various aspects of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preamble of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The Preamble serves as the introductory statement and reflects the vision and philosophy of the Constitution.
 
• It declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and ensures Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity for its citizens.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• Passed in 1976, this amendment brought major changes to the Constitution, including provisions for Fundamental Duties.
 
• It expanded the Directive Principles of State Policy and curtailed judicial review in certain areas.
 
 
 
• **Secularism in India:**
 
 
• Indian secularism ensures equal treatment of all religions without endorsing or discriminating against any specific religion.
 
• It is different from Western secularism, which often involves a strict separation between religion and state.
 
 
 
• **Socialism in India:**
 
 
• Indian socialism emphasizes reducing economic inequalities and ensuring equitable distribution of resources.
 
• It allows for a mix of public and private sectors while focusing on welfare policies for marginalized groups.
